attacks.claim: The plan makes a proprietary vendor sync (server only as hosted Cirrus Cloud) the sole backend in 5.0 and archives stride-server. This directly breaks the README/charter promise that users can self-host sync and own their data, stranding ~3,000 self-hosted instances.
attacks.evidence: "the server component is available only as the hosted Cirrus Cloud service"; "Cirrus Cloud becomes the single sync backend and the stride-server Docker image is archived."

attacks.claim: No exit strategy from Cirrus: closed binary SDK under a commercial license, hosted-only server, and a free tier that the vendor can change. 90k of 100k devices leaves little headroom.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: data portability, exit path, or pricing-change contingency; "our 90k fits the free tier"

attacks.claim: Distributing a prebuilt closed commercial binary inside an MIT open-source app needs license-compatibility review (including F-Droid/open-source distribution expectations). No review is planned, and the plan breaks a charter commitment.
attacks.evidence: "distributed as a prebuilt binary (iOS xcframework, Android AAR) under the Cirrus commercial license"; ABSENT: license review

attacks.claim: All workout data including GPS tracks moves to a third-party processor, a change for users who self-hosted for privacy. There is no disclosure, consent, DPA, or residency statement. Deletion also relies on the vendor admin API with a 30-day window and no confirmation.
attacks.evidence: "Cirrus replicates to Cirrus Cloud"; "via the Cirrus admin API within 30 days"; ABSENT: consent/DPA/residency

attacks.claim: The central claim that Cirrus fixes partial uploads and duplicate-on-retry is unprototyped. The spike is in week 1 of an already-dispatched 5-week build, with no idempotency or dedupe design shown, so the whole architecture rests on an unverified assumption.
attacks.evidence: "Week 1: Cirrus integration spike"; "a dropped connection never leaves a partial workout"

attacks.claim: Downgrade restore from stride-backup-v3.db loses all post-migration workouts written to the Cirrus store, and there is no reverse path from Cirrus to SQLite/REST. Archiving the server in 5.0 is a one-way door.
attacks.evidence: "3.x detects stride-backup-v3.db and restores from it"; ABSENT: reverse migration path

attacks.claim: No budget or cap for exceeding the free tier. Growth past 100k devices or a price change is unplanned spend, and the plan has no figure for it.
attacks.evidence: "free up to 100k monthly active devices"; ABSENT: cost above free tier

attacks.claim: 90-day tombstone retention is shorter than a plausible offline period, so a long-offline device can resurrect deleted workouts. The interaction between append-only-after-finish, per-field LWW, and deletes is unspecified.
Backup deletion requires two successful syncs, so users who never sync keep the backup indefinitely. There is also no sync/migration failure observability beyond the crash-free gate.
attacks.evidence: "deleted only after 30 days and two successful syncs"; "halting if crash-free sessions drop below 99.3%"

attacks.claim: The plan trades away self-hosting, a core value for a segment of users, for reliability, with no research or opt-in. Maintaining legacy REST only until 5.0 leaves self-hosters a deprecation path with no replacement.
attacks.evidence: "Legacy REST sync is removed in app 5.0"; ABSENT: self-hoster consultation

attacks.claim: Auth, key storage, and encryption for Cirrus Cloud and the deletion admin API are not described.
Running two sync protocols behind a flag adds test burden to a small team in 5 weeks.
No UI for pending/queued-offline sync state or migration progress, the very state behind the original complaints; accessibility of these states is also unspecified.
